channel.title: Wire — Frontend
channel.description: Frontend from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: Chrome's team has backed Mozilla's stance
item.description: Google's Chrome for Developers team today supported Mozilla's complaint about Apple's rules on non-WebKit browser engines in the European Union, calling out restrictions that make launching an alternative engine too difficult. (1 source: frontendfocus)

item.title: says it's in talks with Apple
item.description: The European Commission is in talks with Apple over rules that developers say stop them from offering browsers powered by their own technology on the iPhone. (1 source: frontendfocus)

item.title: Understanding CSS random()
item.description: There's been a lot of people talking about how exciting CSS random() is and also plenty mentioning how they're struggling to understand it. (1 source: frontendfocus)

item.title: The beauty of CSS mixins
item.description: CSS mixins let you reuse whole blocks of declarations, not just values. Here is how they work, and a Zen Garden-style experiment that uses them as theming extension points. (1 source: lobsters)

item.title: Browser tabs as a container runtime
item.description: tl;dr tabc is a container runtime, like runc, that runs each container in a Chromium tab. docker run --runtime tabc alpine works and starts in under a second. On a Mac it needs no hypervisor and no Linux VM; Linux for everyone! (1 source: lobsters)

item.title: Foxit Compares 10 HTML to PDF APIs
item.description: Compare 10 HTML to PDF APIs on engine, JavaScript handling, and billing to see what one render will really cost you. (1 source: frontendfocus)
